solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Doctor's order almost received by another doctor

indicators.note: something received is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: an edict is an official order; only its first four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction is passed along and accepted by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, a medical officer, is standard crossword shorthand for a doctor; the definition and the outer piece are both doctors on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal word for a physician or medical student, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Least charitable about holy person earning scrutiny?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: mean means stingy, so meanest is least generous
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: The stingiest person is scornful of a saint's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Earning scrutiny is read as scrutiny of earnings, a cryptic hint flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test examines a person's income and assets to decide eligibility for state benefits.

clue.text: Artist succeeded, getting on towards the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving towards the top means reading the letters upwards, so backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: A painter who made it, achieving success as he grew older and rose to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter famous for ballet dancers, an example of an artist.

clue.text: My ideal place — it's found by the coast

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
a niche is a perfectly suited position

explanation.surface: Someone declares their perfect spot is down by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: My is an exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road running along a cliff edge or seafront, so it lies beside the shore.

clue.text: Lark's flight, gathering wings in abroad

indicators.note: to gather something is to draw it into yourself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: flight in the sense of running away

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A songbird's migration takes it overseas, flapping its wings as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes lark a bird; it is a prank or bit of fun, and flight means fleeing, not flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a carefree adventure or bit of mischief, which is exactly what an escapade is.

clue.text: Showing conviction of criminal breaking in, Feds felt excited

indicators.note: a burglar breaking in gets inside, so one piece enters the middle of the other
excited letters are stirred up and agitated, so they settle in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: FBI agents are thrilled when a burglar is caught breaking in, enough to secure a conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: Conviction suggests a court verdict, but here it means sureness.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-confident means assured of one's own abilities, which is to act with firm belief or conviction.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts bachelor's put away

indicators.note: to put something away is to remove it from sight, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A single man has eaten up his fruit and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruit and nuts reads as a snack, but nuts means crazy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the name for the pineapple in many languages and an old English word for it.

clue.text: Recorded work in car with caution, gripping wheel

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it tightly within, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
a referee books a player when giving a caution
a wheel is round, the shape of the letter

explanation.surface: Driving carefully, both hands on the steering wheel, while recording some work.
explanation.walkthrough: AUDI and BOOK together surround O, giving AUDIOBOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiobook is a spoken recording of a book, so a literary work that has been recorded.

clue.text: Fish guzzler's sorrow after missing starter

indicators.note: missing its starter means the opening letter is gone

parts.note: regret means sorrow or remorse

explanation.surface: A glutton for seafood feels sad after skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter suggests the first course of a meal; it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like wading bird that feeds on fish, making it a consumer of fish.

clue.text: Country song containing line for one on the rebound

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
containing means holding inside, so the song wraps around the other letters

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
L is the abbreviation for line
for one means for example, EG, which is turned round

explanation.surface: A country-and-western song with a line about someone dating again after a breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: Country song looks like one genre; country is the definition and song a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a nation in North Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: What Moscow beggar may do, crossing certain junction, is take risks

indicators.note: crossing here means having something cut across the middle, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: the Russian currency is the rouble, so a beggar there would plead for one
a T-junction, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A Russian vagrant begging at a busy crossroads is courting danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for trouble is an idiom for acting in a way likely to bring harm, so to court danger.

clue.text: Lover, maybe one who's inclined to embrace daughter

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: someone who leans is inclined at an angle
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A romantic partner who tends to hug a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero, so 'maybe' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander is the famous mythical lover of Hero, so he is an example of a lover.

clue.text: Compilers in transport getting reduced fare from Asia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
reduced means cut down, so the vessel loses its last letter

parts.note: a ship is a means of transport; it loses its final letter
the setters of the crossword referring to themselves as us

explanation.surface: The puzzle setters on a cut-price ticket for a trip from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare and transport suggest travel prices, but fare is food here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, food that originates in Asia.

clue.text: Abandon a bit of boxing for a bit of footie

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up
taken as written
a bout is a single boxing contest

explanation.surface: Giving up on boxing to play a little football instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Footie is British slang for football (soccer).
explanation.definitionFit: A kickabout is an informal, casual game of football, just a little play rather than a match.

clue.text: Unable to take off bra? Undo the elastic

indicators.note: elastic material stretches out of shape, so the letters before it are pulled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: Struggling to remove a bra, someone is told to undo the elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Take off suggests undressing; it means leaving the ground, as an aircraft does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earthbound is confined to the ground and cannot fly up from it.

clue.text: Make children soldiers for fascist leader

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
pro means in favour of
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini

explanation.surface: A dictator conscripting children into the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce is to have offspring, which is to produce young of one's own.

clue.text: Clothing for panto with navy blue material

indicators.note: clothing is what covers the outside, so only the edge letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A costume for a pantomime made from navy-blue cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British family Christmas stage show; blue here means smutty, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is an idiom for indecent or sexually explicit, so blue material is pornography.

clue.text: With butterflies on the move, rely on us to capture five

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other
letters on the move are moving about, so they end up in a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Collectors on a field trip count on us to catch five butterflies.
explanation.walkthrough: Butterflies sound like insects to be caught; having butterflies is an idiom for feeling anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Having butterflies in your stomach means feeling jittery, so doing something with them is acting anxiously.

clue.text: Rishi welcoming step that's ultramodern

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a rishi is a Hindu sage or seer
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A politician named Rishi welcomes a forward-looking policy move.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi looks like a reference to Rishi Sunak, the former UK prime minister; it is the Hindu word for a holy wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something very advanced or futuristic, a synonym for highly modern.

clue.text: Appearance of an unwanted character in party politics

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A disliked figure turning up in the world of party politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter or symbol, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing error, where a wrong letter or symbol appears in text.

clue.text: Better to reveal everything, perhaps, in this game?

definitions.text: Better to reveal everything, perhaps, in this game?

parts.note: surface reading: is honesty the best policy, coming clean about it all; setter's reading: a better is someone who places bets, who in this card game may end up naked

explanation.walkthrough: Better is read as one who bets, and revealing everything is literal: in this card game losers shed their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip poker is a poker variant in which losing players remove garments, so a gambler may end up exposing everything.

clue.text: Profiteer has no problem in case of uproar

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a case is the outer shell, so just the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of the word
sure, as in the reply 'no problem!'

explanation.surface: A greedy businessman calmly handles a public outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant interest, taking unfair gains from borrowers.

clue.text: Uncovers bum note playing something with a bit of sparkle

definitions.text: something with a bit of sparkle

parts.note: to moon is to bare your bottom at someone

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it, so the letters of note change order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bares their backside while playing a wrong note in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum is British slang for bottom, and mooning means showing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonstone is a gem with a pearly, shimmering sheen, so it has some sparkle.

clue.text: Underground resistance interrupts feminist movement briefly

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the movement's name is dropped

parts.note: MeToo is the campaign against sexual harassment; it loses its last letter
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An underground resistance group disrupts a women's campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Underground resistance suggests a secret movement; underground is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground railway system in a city, such as the Paris Métro.

clue.text: American's phone ring — it may produce a tune

parts.note: Americans call a mobile phone a cell
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: An American mobile with a ringtone that plays a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Phone ring and tune suggest a ringtone; the definition is a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a bowed string instrument, and instruments are played to make melodies.

clue.text: Allowed on a lake

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Permission is granted to go out on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: On looks like a preposition, but in cricket the on side and leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means permitted by law, so something legal is allowed.

clue.text: Straight guy, one found in a cage

parts.note: true in the sense of straight or level
to guy someone is to mock or tease them, as is to rib

explanation.surface: An honest or heterosexual man ends up locked in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy is a verb, not a man, and the cage is the ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: A true rib is one of the upper rib bones joined directly to the breastbone, part of the ribcage.

clue.text: Taser a criminal, without good means to suppress disorder

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Using a stun gun on a lawbreaker, not a good way to control a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Without is read as outside, not lacking; the rearranged letters wrap around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is used by police to disperse rioting crowds, a way to quell unrest.

clue.text: Running drug, possibly dangerous sort of bandit

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
E is ecstasy
someone armed carries a weapon and may be dangerous

explanation.surface: A fleeing outlaw on drugs, potentially carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine, so the bandit is not a criminal at all.
explanation.definitionFit: One-armed describes the slot machine nicknamed a bandit for its lever and the money it takes.

clue.text: Phosphorus included by hand on another match

indicators.note: something included by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to relay a message is to pass it on
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemical element is handed along to be used in yet another match.
explanation.walkthrough: Phosphorus and match point to matchsticks; the match is a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a game played again after a draw, so it is another match between the same teams.
